body_ar:
لقد حذر الله سبحانه وتعالى ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الفرقة والتحزب والتشيع، ودعا المؤمنين إلى الاعتصام بحبل الله جميعاً، وبين أسباب الفرقة والاختلاف والتناحر، وأنه يجب على المسلم نبذها واجتنابها. وهناك أمور وقع الاختلاف فيها بين الصحابة فمن بعدهم، وهي اجتهادات ينبغي ألا تكون سبباً للفرقة، وأن يعذر المجتهد فيها باجتهاده كما عذره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.
تحذير الله سبحانه ورسوله من الفرقة والاختلاف:
الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى حذر من الشقاق والفرقة في كتابه في العدد من الآيات، وجعله منافياً للرحمة في قوله تعالى: وَلا يَزَالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ* إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ رَبُّكَ [هود:118-119]...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God, glorified and exalted is He, and His Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace, warned against splitting apart, against forming factions and against partisanship, and called the believers to hold fast all together to the rope of God. They set out the causes of splitting apart, of disagreement and of mutual strife, and that it is obligatory upon the Muslim to cast them off and to keep away from them. And there are matters over which disagreement arose among the Companions and among those after them; these are exercises of independent legal reasoning (ijtihād), which ought not to be a cause of splitting apart, and one who exercises such reasoning in them ought to be excused on account of his reasoning, as the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, excused him.

## God's warning, and His Messenger's, against splitting apart and disagreement

Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: God, glorified and exalted is He, warned against discord and splitting apart in His Book in a number of verses, and made it incompatible with mercy in His words, exalted is He: {And they will not cease to differ, except those on whom your Lord has mercy} (Sūrat Hūd 11:118-119) …

flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis after the first proof-text, so that the causes of splitting apart, and the excusing of those who reason differently — the substance the synopsis announces — are never reached. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/g-16.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words

flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.arabic: وهي اجتهادات ينبغي ألا تكون سبباً للفرقة، وأن يعذر المجتهد فيها باجتهاده
flags.context: the site's synopsis, on matters the Companions differed over
options: exercises of independent legal reasoning (ijtihād), … and one who exercises such reasoning ought to be excused on account of his reasoning
matters of juristic judgement, and the jurist should be excused for his judgement
these are opinions, and the one who holds them should be excused
flags.note: The most consequential claim in the record and one the served text never argues. It states a principle — that a qualified scholar who reaches a different conclusion by independent legal reasoning is excused and that such differences must not divide the community — and grounds it in the Prophet's own practice. 'اجتهاد' and 'مجتهد' are fixed in the glossary and must not be reduced to 'opinion' or 'view', which would empty the principle of its technical force: the excuse attaches to qualified reasoning, not to disagreement as such. The whole of it sits in the site's synopsis; the transcribed lesson stops long before it, so it must not be presented as the Sheikh's own stated position.

flags.context: throughout the synopsis and the heading
options: splitting apart, forming factions, partisanship / disagreement
flags.note: Four distinct words in the source and the English keeps four. 'التشيع' is rendered 'partisanship' and NOT 'Shi'ism': the word means taking a party and is used here in a list of general vices alongside 'التحزب', with no sect in view. Rendering it as the name of a sect would turn a warning about factionalism into a sectarian attack, in a record that contains nothing of the kind. Note also that the synopsis uses 'الاختلاف' in the blameworthy sense while also treating the Companions' differences as excusable, which is the tension the lesson presumably resolves in the part that is missing.

options: read a transcription error for في عدد من الآيات
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, style guide section 11. 'في العدد من الآيات' with the definite article is not idiomatic; the expected phrase is 'في عدد من الآيات', 'in a number of verses'. The English gives the evident sense and the Arabic is preserved unrepaired.

flags.arabic: وَلا يَزَالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ* إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ رَبُّكَ [هود:118-119]
options: reproduce the citation and its verse marker as served
normalise the marker and the reference
flags.note: The asterisk in the Arabic is the source's verse separator, falling between 11:118 and 11:119, and the quotation crosses the two verses as the reference says. It has not been carried into the English, where the sense runs on. Note that the Sheikh's point turns on the exception clause, which is the second verse: difference is the human condition except for those given mercy.

translator_notes: One of a run of nine records, IDs 725-733, in the Islamic-thought section, all uploaded on 10 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lecture, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/g-* series, numbered g-16 to g-24 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lecture was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The first record of the Islamic-thought run. Its subject overlaps closely with record 707 of the creed run and with record 731 of this run ('فقه الخلاف'), and the three should be read together once the full texts are in.
'يجب على المسلم نبذها' in the synopsis is rendered 'it is obligatory upon the Muslim to cast them off', per the fixed mapping. It is the site's word and not the Sheikh's.
